headline: High-risk shared filesystem and shell/network defaults make Plandex dangerous with pdf.js outputs; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but still plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pdf.js ingests PDF files and can run browsers, so attacker-controlled PDF content could be rendered into outputs that Plandex may read from the project directory or stdin/stdout. Plandex has broad filesystem access and review-then-apply workflows, so a malicious document could influence downstream instructions. The shared channel is plausible, though not proven by docs.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is copied into Plandex prompts or plan files
IF a PDF contains instruction-like text that survives extraction
IF Plandex auto-applies or trusts extracted text without review
mitigations: Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Keep pdf.js outputs in a separate folder from Plandex inputs
Manually inspect extracted text before reuse
Strip instruction-like boilerplate from PDF text
Use a one-way export format with no embedded prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: pdf.js handles PDF documents, while Plandex reads and writes the project directory with broad network egress and model-provider calls. If sensitive PDF contents are placed into the shared workspace, Plandex can ingest them and transmit context to third parties. This is a default-path leakage risk when both tools share files, even though pdf.js itself has no network egress.
conditions: IF PDF documents containing sensitive data are stored in the same workspace Plandex reads
IF Plandex sends that workspace content to a model provider
IF the project directory is synced or backed up outside the local machine
mitigations: Store PDFs outside the Plandex project directory
Redact sensitive fields before extraction
Disable syncing for the workspace
Use a separate local-only workspace for pdf.js
Review outbound prompts before model calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: pdf.js supports multiple instances and writes PDF-file outputs, while Plandex can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses with shared state via its backend. If both operate on the same directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide, corrupting work or overwriting changes. The overlap is dangerous by default in shared workspaces.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same project directory
IF Plandex auto-applies changes while pdf.js writes or updates files
IF git state is used as the coordination boundary
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Commit or stash before switching agents
Disable auto-apply during concurrent work
Use file locks or a single-writer workflow

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js produces document-processing outputs, and Plandex is a coding agent that can act on files and shell commands. If Plandex treats extracted text or summaries from pdf.js as authoritative, errors in extraction can cascade into incorrect code or file changes. Plandex has review-then-apply safeguards, but they are not guaranteed to verify pdf.js outputs.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is used as the sole source for Plandex actions
IF Plandex does not re-open the original PDF for verification
IF extracted text contains OCR or layout errors
mitigations: Require a second-pass verification against the original PDF
Keep extracted text and source PDF side by side
Use review mode instead of auto-apply
Add a checklist for citations and page numbers
Reject actions based on unverified summaries

E_compliance.rationale: pdf.js is open-source document processing with no stated residency or retention constraints, while Plandex handles source code and model-provider API keys with broad network egress. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, but Plandex's outbound calls can create compliance gaps if regulated PDF data is introduced. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their interaction.
conditions: IF regulated PDF data is processed in the shared workspace
IF model-provider calls receive that data
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to the project
mitigations: Keep regulated PDFs out of Plandex workflows
Use a local-only model path where possible
Minimize logged prompt content
Document retention settings before processing
Delete temporary extraction artifacts promptly
